column15: Single product, no information found this session; generic surname brand, too ambiguous to guess anything further
No web presence found this session; own-label, origin unclear despite the IE country guess from the catalogue.

Sample "Hepp Tharcis Alsacien" suggests an Alsatian (France) distiller (Hepp is a known Alsace fruit-spirit/eau-de-vie house); could not confirm within budget whether they produce whisky specifically or its peat status - left unknown.

No web presence found; own-label, could not confirm this is genuine whisky vs. another Spanish spirit category. Catalogue guesses blend/ES; kept (unlike 'Haran', see report) since nothing here explicitly signals a non-whisky oak-chip product.

Organic-certified Scotch whisky brand; recalled to be French-marketed but official sites (highlandharvest.se/.fr) did not resolve this session, so ownership and peat character could not be confirmed by citation. Source distillery undisclosed. Left peat unknown per policy rather than rely on memory.

Single-product brand; could not identify a source this session (WebSearch budget exhausted). "Hinotori" (火鳥, "firebird") is an unambiguous Japanese word, so countryCode is guessed as JP on that basis alone - this guess is NOT backed by a citation and peatProfile is correctly left unknown; a reviewer should verify the brand entirely.
No information found within budget. Single sample 'Hogs 3' gives no clear indication of style, origin or the meaning of '3'.

Catalogue's own product name states the producer directly ("House of Maclair Ian Macleod"). Ian Macleod Distillers is confirmed real (Wikipedia), but this specific range is not among the brands the article lists (Isle of Skye, Sheep Dip, Pig's Nose, King Robert II, etc.), so peat is left unknown rather than inherit the parent company's other house styles.
No citable source found this session for this Irish whiskey despite the name being familiar; left unknown rather than rely on memory.

Brand string as catalogued ("Irishamerican", one word) is unusual and its single sample name is just "Irish" - possibly a mangled "Irish American" blend, possibly a plain Irish whiskey; leaning Irish whiskey (categorically unpeated) but genuinely uncertain, low confidence.

Single product "J.Riddle Peated" - could not identify a producer within budget. The product name itself asserts "Peated" but I found no independent source to cite, so left peatProfile=unknown rather than assert heavy/medium on the strength of the catalogue name alone (brief rule: never invent a citation). REVIEWER FLAG: name strongly implies a peated whisky - worth a manual peatProfile assignment once the producer is identified.

First Georgian whisky, Kartveli Distillery (founder Jimsher Chkhaidze). "Tsinandali" in the catalogue sample name is a wine-cask finish (aged in ex-Tsinandali-wine barrels), not a separate product or a wine product - this is genuinely a whisky. No peat/smoke mentioned; matured in Georgian wine and brandy casks. defaultTypeName left empty - only one expression researched, described as "blended" but full range unconfirmed

Not researched (budget). Sample "Johnny Hepp Alsacien" names Alsace explicitly; countryCode inferred from the name only. A real Alsatian spirits house named Hepp exists but this was not confirmed this session.
Band-branded novelty whisky ("50 Heavy Metal Years"); origin not identified, no search performed this pass.

Closed distillery (mothballed 2000, demolished 2016), Miyota, Nagano Prefecture. Peat level of the original production was not confirmed by the research done here (found only that a newly revived operation reportedly plans both peated and unpeated malt in future) - left unknown rather than guessed. Named in Artist series samples (this batch).

Confirmed premium single malt Irish whiskey brand, produced by Irish Distillers (Pernod Ricard), introduced 1998, named for Knappogue Castle in County Clare. Source distillery undisclosed for current releases; kind=blend used as the closest available bucket for an undisclosed-origin single-malt label (rule 3 in the brief), not because it is blended-type whiskey. peatProfile via general Irish-whiskey category fact.
Catalogue spells the brand simply "Koriyama"; the operating distillery's formal name is Asaka Distillery, in Kōriyama, Fukushima Prefecture, founded 2016. No peat information found.
Single product, just "Kyoda". Wikipedia search returns nothing relevant (only an unrelated anime director's surname). No basis found for country, category or peat.

No web presence found for this whisky (zero Wikipedia hits). The name recalls the Belgian 'Lambertus' beer brand (Brouwerij Huyghe) but no whisky connection is confirmed; left entirely unknown rather than guessed.

No web presence found this session. Sole sample "Hiberum Saboga" suggests a Latin/Hibernia (Ireland) theme while "Lehmann" reads German/French/Alsatian - conflicting signals, country and peat left unknown rather than guessed.

Denver, Colorado craft distillery, known for Maryland-style rye whiskey per Wikipedia's List of whisky brands. Sample Leopold Bros Peach is likely a flavored/fruit expression; range spans types so defaultTypeName left empty.
No web presence found; treated as an ordinary own-label blended Scotch per budget policy for one-product long-tail brands.

Could not confirm this session (domain lookups failed, no Wikipedia page). Unconfirmed personal recollection that this may be a French independent bottler of sourced (non-French) malt whisky rather than a French distillery -- flagged for human review rather than acted on without a citation.
